note: Days between regular meetings of a local legislative body, by body type and population band. A place's own recorded charter or council rule is used where one is read; every other body takes the band median below, ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE. No national table of meeting frequency was reachable (ICMA's form-of-government survey does not publish one), so each median rests on the examples cited and is marked estimated. Nothing here picks a meeting for a place at random; the interval is the median of its type and size.

evidence.fact: 90% of the 20 largest California cities meet once weekly; Los Angeles three times a week, San Diego twice.
evidence.source: Legislative Analyst Report, Meeting Schedules, City Councils (File No. 020037), San Francisco Board of Supervisors

evidence.fact: Cities hold an average of 24 meetings a year in a California study (twice a month); mid-sized cities of about 40,000 to 53,000 meet twice a month.
evidence.source: Legislative Analyst Report, File No. 020037; Cupertino, Analysis of City Council Meetings 2017-2024 (February 13, 2025)

evidence.fact: Most Texas cities meet twice a month (Waco, Temple, Abilene); Willis, Texas requires meeting at least once a month.
evidence.supports: city-council 14 for mid-sized places, 30 for the smallest
evidence.source: Killeen Daily Herald, councilman floats reducing council meetings by half; Willis, Texas city code Article III

evidence.fact: Michigan townships of Lincoln, Arcada, Leighton, Frankenmuth and Douglass hold regular board meetings once a month.
evidence.supports: town-or-township-board 30 for small and mid-sized places

gaps: County board cadence rests on the same city examples and no county table was read; larger townships and counties are estimated. Replace a band median with a place's recorded schedule as sources are read.
